title: 1wg9fbc
Rejecting the beatification of Ali, Syiffin and Hakem
hook: While Imam Ali's right was plain, Mu'awiya did not pledge allegiance. At Siffin he fixed the Qur'an to spears.
scenes.0.text: Mu'awiya had been governor of Damascus for some twenty years and had an army loyal to him. He was first appointed governor of Damascus by Umar, and Uthman expanded his jurisdiction. When **Ali** became caliph, he took the governors from whom the people complained, one by one, to ensure justice. He wanted to remove Mu'awiya from the governorship of Damascus. This decision was not a personal account, but a step to correct the governance of the nation. But Mu'awiya refused both the azli and the ba'ath. A pledge of allegiance. The Prophet's guardian did not submit to Ali and did not relinquish his power. Damascus did not recognize the bequest made in Medina.
scenes.1.text: Mu'awiya showed the bloodstained shirt of Uthman in the Damascus mosque to incite the people against **Ali**. Mu'awiya was using Uthman's blood as an excuse. But his real aim was not justice, but to delay the beatification and preserve his power in Damascus. When Ali's caliphate was accepted in Medina, he avoided beatification by putting forward a bloody shirt. That shirt had become a political shield, not a mourning one.
scenes.2.text: **Ali** wrote letters to Mu'awiya in Damascus and sent envoys. He demanded that he be sworn in first, then that Uthman's blood account be questioned in court with justice. The Ummah proposed a trial in an orderly manner, before the split. But the Deputy didn't take it. Before making the bead, he demanded that Uthman's killers be handed over to him. Finally, in the 37th year of the Exodus, the two armies came face-to-face in the plain of Sinear on the Euphrates. Ali tried the pen before the sword, the word before the battle. The side that chose the war became the Deputy.
scenes.3.text: Mu'awiya's army, the first to reach **Siffin**, seized the Euphrates bank and cut off **Ali**'s troops. Finally, Ali's troops captured the riverbank. This time the water was in the hands of Ali. But Ali did not retaliate and allowed the people of Damascus to take water from the river. He even gave water to his enemy. Years later, on the banks of the same Euphrates, the army of Yazid, the son of Mu'awiya, would see the children of Husayn, the son of Ali, even a sip of water.
scenes.4.text: The elderly Sahabi **Ammar b. Yasir**, who fought with Ali in Siffin, was martyred. The Prophet had foretold years ago that he would be killed by a group of Ba'athists. The baqi means the side that rebels against the legitimate imam. The group that killed Ammar was Muawi's army. This hadith goes for Buhari and Muslim. Ammar's death caused great unrest in the Damascus army. When the hadith of Amr b. al-As reminded Mu'awiya, Mu'awiya said, "Did we kill him? Those who brought him here killed him", he tried to blame it on Ali. But the Prophet's word was clear, and Ammar had died on the side of Ali.
scenes.5.text: When the battle turned in **Ali**'s favor and the Damascus army was about to be defeated, on Amr b. al-As's suggestion, the Damascus soldiers put the pages of the Quran on the tip of their spears. They shouted, "Let the Book of God judge between us". This was not worship, it was a deception, and Ali immediately said it was a deception, and called upon his army to continue the battle. But a group in his army refused to fight under the pretext of mushafs and forced Ali to stop the fight. Victory, when the Koran was on the point of the spears, escaped. The party who was about to be defeated took the Book of Allah as a shield.
scenes.6.text: Abu Musa al-Eshari represented **Ali**'s side in the arbitration, while Amr b. al-As represented Mu'awiya's side. According to the popular narrative, the two judges appeared in front of the crowd. First, Abu Musa took off the ring from his finger. Removing the ring was to announce that Ali was no longer the caliph. Then Amr b. al-As stood up and put his ring on his finger. To wear the ring was to proclaim Mu'awiya as caliph. The reliability of this narrative is questionable, and the sentences spoken vary from story to story. Ali did not accept this result, because the spear trick had persisted in the arbitral tribunal.
scenes.7.text: After the referee, **Ali**'s ranks split and Mu'awiya increased his attacks. One of Ali's most trusted people during this period was Malik al-Eshter. Malik was Ali's most loyal commander. He fought at the front of the army in the war and was known in the administration as a trustworthy statesman. Ali sent him to Egypt as governor. Malik was poisoned on the way to Kulzum. An official was bribed and the poison was mixed with honey. When news of this reached Damascus, the people rejoiced. It is said that Mu'awiya said that one of Ali's two arms was cut off at Siffin with Ammar, and the other now. Mu'awiya then conquered Egypt and the governor Muhammad b. Abi Bekir was killed. **Busr b. Ertat** shed blood in the Hejaz and Yemen. In the 40th year of the Hijrah, Ali was martyred during one of the morning prayers in Kufa.
sunni.0.says: The Prophet's saying about Ammar, «a rebellious group will kill you».
sunni.1.says: The same hadith; the group that will kill Ammar.
sunni.2.says: Amr b. al-As reminding Mu'awiya of the hadith; the answer «those who brought him killed him».
sunni.3.says: The bank of the Euphrates, the raising of the mushafs, the Arbitration and the later events.
sunni.4.says: Tells of Siffin and the Arbitration in detail; also states that Imam Ali was closer to the right.
shia.0.says: A detailed account of Siffin; the seizing of the Euphrates and the tying of the mushafs to spears.
shia.1.says: Imam Ali's letters to Mu'awiya and his sermons on Siffin.
shia.2.says: Mu'awiya's stance toward Imam Ali and his role at Siffin.
disputes.0.title: y3yzlx
Why was allegiance not given?
disputes.0.sunni: That Mu'awiya did not give allegiance is told in both traditions. The Sunni majority understands his reason as the blood of Caliph Uthman, counts this as an error of ijtihad, and finds Imam Ali closer to the right.
disputes.0.shia: That Mu'awiya did not give allegiance is told in both traditions. In the Shia account the aim is power; Ammar's martyrdom also shows standing with Imam Ali.
disputes.1.title: mplnbw
Is there a trick in the Arbitration meeting?
disputes.1.sunni: The Arbitration meeting is told in both traditions. Amr's trick comes through the channel of Abu Mikhnaf, and many Sunni scholars look at the detail with caution.
disputes.1.shia: The Arbitration meeting is told in both traditions. In the Shia account Imam Ali was against this from the start and had said that the mushafs were a trick.
questions.0: Ali used to say, "First order, then trial". Why do you think Ali put off the case until after it was settled?
questions.1: The Prophet had announced that Ammar would be killed by a group of rebels, and Ammar was martyred alongside Ali. How do you think this news makes a difference in Siffin?
questions.2: Ali immediately said that the guards were a trick. Why do you think some of his army refused to fight when the scouts attacked them with spears?
summary: Mu'awiya refused allegiance. At Siffin Ammar was martyred beside Imam Ali. The mushafs were hung on spears and the Arbitration divided the army. Then Egypt was taken, Muhammad b. Abi Bakr was killed, and Malik al-Ashtar was poisoned on the road. Imam Ali was martyred in 40 AH.
key: The governor who did not give allegiance: Siffin, the mushafs and the Arbitration
notes.0: When Imam Ali dismissed him, Mu'awiya did not give up the governorship of Syria and did not give allegiance.
notes.1: He cited the blood of Caliph Uthman as the reason.
notes.2: At Siffin Ammar b. Yasir was martyred; the Prophet's hadith «a rebellious group will kill him» was recalled (Bukhari 447, Muslim 2915).
notes.3: As the war turned in Imam Ali's favor the mushafs were tied to spears and the Arbitration was accepted.
notes.4: Afterward Egypt was taken, Muhammad b. Abi Bakr was killed, and Malik al-Ashtar was poisoned on the road.
